title: Receipts distinguish selected focus from execution ownership
outcome: Receipts distinguish selected focus from execution ownership
acceptance: a test issues two concurrent adds through one session followed by an implicit-target operation and proves the returned refs are independent of completion order and the implicit target is the documented one

A completed, cancelled, or superseded item may remain the selected navigation focus until an explicit focus-setting operation changes it; receipts name its terminal lifecycle separately from live execution ownership, no successor is selected automatically, and a terminal run never supplies a live control binding.

next, show, and refusal texts name the focused item and the claim holder as two distinct facts, so a session with a focus but no claim is never told it holds the work and a holder is never told it lacks focus

read words (show, ls, next, search, memories) never change the session focus; a mutation given an explicit ref never consults focus; add's receipt names the focus it set; docs state that implicit targets are unsafe under concurrent use of one session

completion.summary: Receipts keep selected focus apart from execution ownership: add discloses the focus it set (focus_change); agent show and its notes/history first page carry session_focus apart from the holder; a completed, cancelled or superseded focus stays selected without ownership, successor or control binding; concurrent adds each get their own result; docs say implicit targets follow the last committed focus-setting call. Landed in 3abe2b2 (bundle 10 changeset 3).
